headline: Recommended a $1 sale of Centre Square parcel 30-1 to Carrier Construction; approved Integrity Manufacturing site plan for Lot 6 in Southeast Bristol Business Park.
summary: Carrier Construction would buy parcel 30-1 on North Main Street for $1 and keep it as a civic space. The recommendation includes an Enterprise Zone tax abatement and further review. Lot 6 in the Southeast Bristol Business Park was approved for a site plan and referred for a $156,000 sale to Integrity Manufacturing.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the August 6, 2026 regular meeting. Commissioner Schmelder abstained. All in favor.
Approved the Consent Agenda with no items pulled for discussion. All in favor.

Recommended selling Centre Square parcel 30-1 on North Main Street to Carrier Construction for $1, with an Enterprise Zone tax abatement, and referred it to the Planning Commission and City Council Real Estate Committee. All in favor.
Accepted the Downtown Update report. All in favor.
Accepted the Grants Update and Grants Management Software report. All in favor.
Forwarded to the Board of Finance a request to transfer $15,000 from the Economic Development Expenses Account to the Façade Grant Account. All in favor.
Approved the site plan and building elevation plan for Integrity Manufacturing’s new 23,100 square foot building on Lot 6. All in favor.

Approved a motion requiring staff to report on final construction of Lot 6, including signage and landscaping, to ensure alignment with the Southeast Bristol Business Park Design Guidelines and Regulations. All in favor.

Referred the sale of Lot 6 in the Southeast Bristol Business Park to Integrity Manufacturing for $156,000 to the City Council, with steps by the Planning Commission and City Council Real Estate Committee. All in favor.

plain_text:
ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT 
Thursday, September 3, 2026, 2026 at 5:00pm 
City Council Chambers, City Hall, 111 N. Main Street & on Zoom 
 
 
Present:  Mayor Zoppo-Sassu -- Chair, Howard Schmelder -- Vice Chair (Zoom), City 
Council Member Susan Tyler, Commissioners Dave Mills, Marvin (Mickey) 
Goldwasser, Tom Hick (Zoom), LaQuita Kearney-Gonzales, and Louise 
Provenzano (Zoom) 
 
Absent:  Commissioner Jason Paul Sirko 
 
ECD Staff:  Justin Malley - Executive Director, Dr. Dawn Leger - Grants Administrator 
 
Guests: Charlie Talmadge – President, Development Planning Solutions 
 
I. Call to Order 
Mayor Zoppo-Sassu called the meeting to order at 5:00pm and led all present in 
the Pledge of Allegiance.  
 
II. Public Participation 
There was no Public Participation. 
 
III. Approval of Minutes 
A. Minutes of the August 6, 2026 Regular Meeting 
The mayor called for a motion to approve the Minutes from the August 6, 2026 
Meeting. The motion to approve was made by Commissioner Mills and 
seconded by Commissioner Goldwasser. There were no edits or corrections 
noted. All were in favor and the Minutes were accepted into the record. 
Commissioner Schmelder abstained from the vote as he had not been present 
at the August Meeting. 
 
IV.         Consent Agenda 
A.  Communications 
B.  Economic Development/Grants/Marketing Report 
The mayor called for a motion to approve the Consent Agenda. Commissioner 
Goldwasser made the motion to approve which was seconded by City Council
Member Tyler. No items were noted for discussion. All were in favor and the 
Consent Agenda was accepted into the record. 
 
V.      New Business 
A.  Centre Square Parcel Report 
Justin Malley provided information regarding Parcel 30-1 on the corner of N. 
Main Street and Riverside Avenue. This parcel was originally designated to be a 
pocket park for the city per an agreement with the state. Under that agreement, 
the city would fund the build out of publicly accessible green space and parking, 
and maintain the property with no taxes paid by the city. 
 
Carrier is developing the neighboring Parcel 30-3 with a mixed-use building. 
They’ve expressed interest in owning Parcel 30-1 as part of their overall plan for 
the area, and have agreed to retain ownership and maintenance of the parcel as 
a fully designed civic space if approved. Justin Malley advised the Board that 
State approval has been received to sell Parcel 30-1 to Carrier provided they 
agree to the original intended use of the space.  
 
The ECD Board now has the option to approve a motion to sell the property to 
Carrier. The proposed motion indicates the property would likely qualify for the 
Enterprise Zone abatement. Carrier is asking the Board to approve a sale price of 
$1.00 for assuming the obligation to build out and maintain the parcel.  
 
Charlie Talmadge spoke to the Board on behalf of the Carrier project and 
discussion followed including confirmation that the Board viewing site plans for 
the development as part of the approval process. Commissioner Goldwasser 
added that the Downtown Committee identified Carrier’s ownership of Parcel 
30-1 as positive for the city as it would mean keeping the planned use for the 
land and receiving taxes for it while removing the city’s obligation to build it out 
and maintain it 
 
A motion to waive the reading of the proposed Motion, and to approve the 
Motion as written was made by Commissioner Goldwasser and seconded by 
City Council Member Tyler.  
 
The Motion as written reads as follows: 
Motion to recommend Mayor Ellen Zoppo-Sassu, or Acting Mayor, to execute a 
Purchase and Sale Agreement and to complete the property transaction, subject to
the approval of Corporation Counsel, with Carrier Construction Inc. or its assigns 
for the sale and redevelopment of the Centre Square North Main Street property, 
identified as parcel 30-1 on the City land records, for the purchase price of $1 to 
construct a parking area and publicly accessible green space.  
 
Further, pending the legal acquisition of the Centre Square North Main Street 
property identified as parcel 30-1 by Carrier Construction, Inc. or its assigns for 
purposes of developing a parking area and publicly accessible green space, to 
approve the following Enterprise Zone tax abatement: 
 
• Construction Year #1 (period to begin immediately following property closing): 
100% real property tax abatement attributable to the value of property 
improvements. 
• Construction Year #2: 100% real property tax abatement on the value of property 
improvements.  
• Construction Year #3: 100% real property tax abatement on the value of property 
improvements.   
• Year #1 (period to begin following issuance of a certificate of occupancy): 100% 
real property tax abatement on the value of improvements 
• Year #2: 100% real property abatement on the value of improvements. 
• Year #3: 50% real property abatement on the value of improvements. 
• Year #4: 40% real property abatement on the value of improvements. 
• Year #5: 30% real property abatement on the value of improvements. 
• Year #6: 20% real property abatement on the value of improvements. 
• Year #7: 10% real property abatement on the value of improvements.  
 
I further move that this matter be referred to the Planning Commission for 
completion of a C.G.S. 8-24 Report, and to the City Council Real Estate Committee 
for completion of a C.G.S. 7-163e Public Hearing for the sale of municipally owned 
property. 
 
There was no further discussion or questions. All were in favor and the motion 
accepted into the record. 
 
Justin Malley took this moment to introduce City Hall Intern Nick Carmelich to 
the Board. Nick is currently working in conjunction with the Mayor’s Office and 
the ECD Department and is earning his MPA from UCONN. 
 
B. Downtown Update 
JHM Group is the preferred developer for the former JH Sessions building at 273 
Riverside Avenue, and they’re reportedly making steady progress. Their 
architects have been at the property gathering information as part of the floor
plan layout process. JHM is also working with the city’s Corporation Council 
attorneys on the purchase and sale agreement.  
Justin Malley is encouraged by the developer’s progress. Additional coordination 
needs to take place on the State and Federal level. JHM has expressed an 
interest in the use of the TIF Program (Tax Increment Financing) designed for just 
this type of use. Further information about the TIF program will be provided at 
the October Board Meeting.  
 
Sei Bella Restaurant at the former Main Street Pint and Plate location on Main 
Street may open this month. Their exact opening date will be provided when it 
becomes available. Apex Golf has opened in the former Bikers Edge location at 
99 Main Street. It is a member only high end golf instruction facility. Their holding 
an Open House on from 10am to 2pm on Sunday, September 6th. 
 
The mayor mentioned that the Governor visited the city last week. He viewed the 
Route 72/69 intersection improvements and the West End in general. Long-term, 
steady tenancy was recognized, and the Public Works Department cleared the 
landscaping beds as part of an agreement made under the previous 
administration.   
 
Commissioner Goldwasser asked for an update on the former athletic center 
building. The mayor reported that the issue was recently taken up with the Code 
Enforcement Department as the city believes the hazardous materials 
measurement report they were provided with is inappropriate. The city is in the 
process of obtaining an Administrative Warrant to gain access to test materials 
and make a decision when those results are in.  
 
Dr. Dawn Leger reported that the city submitted information to determine site 
eligibility for an EPA assessment grant through NVCOG (Naugatuck Valley 
Council of Governments) for 296 Riverside Avenue. This would be an avenue for 
Phase I and possible Phase II to be completed at that location. 
 
City Council Member Tyler asked about the former Bristol Press location on 
Riverside Avenue next to the new Apex Golf. Justin Malley confirmed that the 
building is available for use. He reports that the space is much improved inside 
as well as with the newly installed windows.
The mayor called for a Motion to accept the Report. The motion was made by 
Commissioner Mills and seconded by City Council Member Tyler. All were in 
favor and the Report was accepted into the record. 
 
C. Grants Update and Grants Management Software 
Dr. Dawn Leger shared an update on the NAA (Neighborhood Assistance Act) 
which is a state initiative that gives corporate business tax credits to companies 
making cash contributions to approved municipal or tax-exempt community 
programs. Bristol is a pass through for the applications and the program is 
through the Department of Revenue Services in Hartford.  
 
Applications for the program come to the city to ensure all the necessary 
materials are in hand, and that requests are appropriate for the program. They 
are then submitted to the State for approval. Dr. Leger reported that all the 
recent applications from Bristol were accepted by the State and included the 
Empowered to Work initiative through BristolWORKS! 
 
Dr. Leger also advised that the city has not yet received the federal funds from 
the CDBG (Community Development Block Grant) for FY52 (Fiscal Year 52). The 
Annual Report was filed on time and approved, as was the CAPER or 
Consolidated Report. It is unclear why the funds have yet to be released to the 
city. 
 
The Residential Rehabilitation Program is steady as it continues to transition 
from a grant to a loan program. There is a waiting list for project requests which 
is indicative of a growing demand and less funding issued to the city each year.  
 
Justin Malley spoke about an opportunity for the city to pursue a dynamic grant 
management software program offered by Avila. This program uses AI to help 
with grant research and writing, and grant management after the fact. A bid 
waiver request was made at the most recent Board of Finance Meeting after 
research into this service indicated that Avila was the only company with the 
product and services offered. Information about the company was provided to 
the Board for review. 
 
The mayor called for a Motion to accept the Report. Commissioner Mills and 
seconded by City Council Member Tyler. All were in favor and the Report was 
accepted into the record.
D. Board of Finance (BOF) Transfer Request 
Justin Malley requested a transfer to build up the Façade Grant fund and allow 
for approximately two new projects to receive this type of grant award. 
 
Commissioner Goldwasser made the following Motion: 
Motion to transfer $15,000 from the Economic Development Expenses Account – 
Account #1044109-589300 – to the Façade Grant Account – Account #1044109-
589335 – and to forward to the Board of Finance for action. 
 
There was no discussion. The motion was seconded by City Council Member 
Tyler. All were in favor and the Motion was accepted into the record. 
 
VI.        New Business by Commissioners 
Commissioner Schmelder spoke to the Carrier’s Haviland Street project and 
encouraged everyone to view the Carrier’s Facebook video where they explain 
the project phases and the grading taking place. On a personal note, the 
Commissioner expressed his thanks to the Board for their condolences and 
prayers at the recent and close passing of two of his family members.  
 
There was no additional New Business by Commissioners. 
 
VII.      Old Business by Commissioners 
There was no Old Business by Commissioners.  
 
The mayor updated the Board regarding the Special Zoning Commission Meeting 
with regard to the moratorium on vape shops. They are forwarding the 
moratorium for consideration as a new amendment in the coming week. The 18-
month moratorium would be applicable to new applications while the city works 
through the new state laws, existing city ordinances, and all impactful 
requirements. 
 
VIII.    Committee Reports 
A. Industrial Committee Report 
Commissioner Mills advised the Board that the Committee had met before the 
Board Meeting to discuss plans for Integrity Manufacturing at Lot #6 in the 
Southeast Bristol Business Park (SEBBP). The Committee would like the Board to 
consider and vote on the proposed Motions as provided.
City Council Member Tyler read the first Motion as follows: 
Motion to approve the site plan and building elevation plan dated July 10, 2026 titled 
“Integrity Manufacturing LLC 190 Business Park Drive” representing the new 
construction project for Integrity Mfg. LLC (dba Integrity High Precision Grinding) 
on Lot 6 of the Southeast Bristol Business Park that includes construction of an 
approximately 23,100 square foot building and 
associated parking/loading area to serve as the headquarters for Integrity High 
Precision Grinding. 
 
There was no discussion. The Motion was seconded by Commissioner Kearney-
Gonzalez. All were in favor and the Motion was accepted into the record. 
 
                    The mayor read the second Motion as follows: 
Motion that Economic and Community Development staff must report to the Economic 
and Community Development Board details on final construction of Lot 6, including 
the mounting of building signage and landscaping, to ensure these activities align with 
the Southeast Bristol Business Park Design Guidelines and Regulations. 
 
There was no discussion. The Motion was seconded by Commissioner 
Goldwasser. All were in favor and the Motion was accepted into the record. 
 
City Council Member Tyler read the third Motion as follows: 
Motion to sell Lot #6 of the Southeast Bristol Business Park at the listed price of 
$156,000 to Integrity Manufacturing LLC (dba Integrity High Precision Grinding) for 
construction of an approximately 23,100 square foot manufacturing facility. 
 
I further move that this matter be referred to the City Council for referral to the 
Planning Commission for completion of a C.G.S. 8-24 Report, and to the City Council 
Real Estate Committee for completion of a C.G.S. 7-163e Public Hearing for the sale 
of municipally owned property. 
 
There was no discussion. The Motion was seconded by Commissioner Kearney-
Gonzalez. All were in favor and the Motion was accepted into the record. 
 
Commissioner Schmelder noted the achievement of all the properties being sold 
in full now and also on the tax rolls.
B. City Council Member Report 
City Council Member Tyler reported on the tangible community support being 
provided in the wake of the Brian’s Angels closure. Through Bristol Cares, all 
community partners in the city have been collaborating to fill in gaps that may 
surface as a result of the closing. St. Vincent DePaul and Meals for Neighbors 
were named as two agencies providing grab-and-go or hot meal services in the 
coming week. 
 
IX.     Adjournment 
With no further discussion, the mayor called for a Motion to adjourn. The motion 
was made by Commissioner Mills and seconded by Commissioner Schmelder. 
All were in favor and the meeting was adjourned at 5:43pm. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Sharon Arsego 
Recording Secretary
